label: Recharge Card
title: Recharge Card
summary: Use a Recharge Card to show one prepaid plan: its price, validity, data, the apps it includes, and the action to buy it.

anatomy.description: A white panel stacks the plan’s name and price, a row of facts, the fine print, and the actions, 20 px apart. The facts row has a third column when the plan includes apps.

configuration.title: Facts, apps, and actions
configuration.description: subscriptionContent adds a third column, Subscriptions, for the apps the plan includes: pass Avatars, and the card overlaps them at size S. Leave it out for two columns. actions takes your Buttons, and the card makes them purple, size S, and Emphasis High; give a second one Emphasis Low, as Figma does. The buttons always split their row into equal widths, so with two, the longer label is cut short. On the card, Button / Size M makes them bigger, and AppearanceBrand and Emphasis change all of them. The card’s own text and panel don’t change with modes.

states.title: Its buttons act, or the whole card does
states.description: The card isn’t pressable: its buttons are. onPress makes the whole card one button, announced by its title, and disabled then stops it firing without changing its look. Use one or the other: a pressable card with actions puts buttons inside a button. The card has no selected or loading state.

sizing.title: At least 312 px wide
sizing.description: The card is never narrower than 312 px, as Figma draws it, and fills a wider host. The facts share the width in equal columns, and the price stays at the left. Height follows the content: 20 px between the rows and 20 px of padding at the top and bottom, 16 px at the sides. Without actions, the empty row still adds 20 px at the bottom.

content.title: A name, a number, and short facts
content.description: Make the title the plan’s name and the price a number: the card adds the ₹. Keep validity and data to one value each, such as 28 days and 2 GB/day; the labels Validity, Data, and Subscriptions are fixed. Put the plan’s limits in the disclaimer, in a line or two of fine print. Label the main action Recharge.

sources.title: Use the public Recharge Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Recharge Card exposes only title and disclaimer as properties; the price, facts, apps, and buttons are layers there. In the package, actions always split their row into equal widths, so of two different labels the longer is cut short (Biscuit’s own Storybook shows “View Det…”), while Figma’s buttons fit their labels. Without actions an empty row still adds space. The card is 271 px tall where Figma’s is 261, because its text lines are taller. The ₹ and the labels Validity, Data, and Subscriptions are fixed, a card without onPress isn’t announced by its title, and disabled has no look of its own. The published Storybook renders every story as a pressable card and still shows the older generated page (all reported).
